    Maps between occurrences of a common substring (Step 2 of Proposition 3.8) #

    If an interval π₁ of the string diagram has no outgoing boundary edges, an interval π₂ has no incoming boundary edges, and the two intervals are matched compatibly with vertices and internal edges, then sending the basis vector at π₂ i to the basis vector at π₁ i (and the others to zero) is an endomorphism of M(w) [Crawley-Boevey, pp. 260--261]. It is nonzero and, when π₂ misses a position, not injective; so a brick admits no such pair (false_of_matched).
